newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Netherlands transfers remaining Fokker shares.
newsitem.headline: Netherlands transfers remaining Fokker shares.

text.p: The Dutch government has transferred its remaining 22 percent stake in bankrupt planemaker Fokker to Daimler Benz Aerospace, the Economic Affairs Ministry said in a letter to parliament Tuesday.

"DASA has exercised an option they have held for three years," a ministry spokesman said, using the popular name for Daimler Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler Benz AG of Germany, which acquired a majority stake in Fokker in 1993.

The spokesman said no money had changed hands in the transaction. He said the transfer of the Dutch state's remaining stake in the planemaker was part of the 1993 rescue deal in which DASA acquired a majority Fokker stake.

It was agreed then that the Dutch government would sell its remaining Fokker shares to DASA at the end of 1996 at a pre-determined price of 121.8 million guilders ($71 million), but that the sale price would be reduced if Fokker performed poorly.
Since Fokker's bankruptcy, the shares have become worthless. The Dutch planemaker was declared bankrupt in March this year, following a decision by DASA in January to cut off further funding.

Since then Fokker has been run by court-appointed administrators who are still in talks with South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries on a possible Samsung takeover of the company's core planemaking business.
